content.value_statement: Email teams can make costly decisions from underpowered or poorly controlled tests. This skill creates a structured experiment plan and interprets results using user-provided campaign data.
actual_capabilities: Selects A/B, multivariate, send-time, or hold-out test modes from the stated goal.
Creates falsifiable hypotheses and variant matrices with controls.
Defines primary metrics, secondary metrics, and deliverability guardrails.
Plans sample size, minimum detectable effect, power, and estimated duration.
Interprets supplied variant counts with effect size, uncertainty, and practical-impact flags.
Returns an undecided outcome when no owner-approved decision rule exists.
limitations: It relies on campaign data, baselines, and business rules supplied by the user.
It does not write email creative or approve a business action independently.
It does not replace legal, privacy, deliverability, or statistical expert review.
The optional local statistics helper must be available and reviewed before command-based calculations.

use_cases.title: Plan a subject-line experiment
use_cases.description: Define a controlled subject-line A/B test with sample size, guardrails, and a read date.

use_cases.title: Assess a completed campaign test
use_cases.description: Interpret delivered, open, click, and conversion counts with statistical and practical effect flags.

use_cases.title: Measure incremental email value
use_cases.description: Create a randomized hold-out plan to evaluate conversion or revenue lift from a send.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: plan an A/B test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an email A/B subject-line test. My baseline open rate is 38%, my list has 12,000 people, and I want to detect a 3-point lift.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: plan a send-time test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a send-time test for our weekly newsletter. Baseline open rate is 40%, the list has 20,000 people, and content must stay constant.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: size a multivariate test
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess whether a factorial design is feasible.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a 2 by 2 subject and CTA experiment. Baseline click rate is 2.1%, send volume is 8,000 per week, alpha is .05, and power is .80.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: read a hold-out result
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this hold-out result using my decision rule. Control: 10,000 delivered and 180 conversions. Variant: 10,000 delivered and 215 conversions. Guardrail unsubscribe rates were 0.12% and 0.13%.

output_examples.input: Plan a subject-line test with a 40% baseline open rate and a 3-point target lift.
output: Primary metric: open rate; guardrails: unsubscribes and spam complaints
Plan: randomize recipients, keep content constant, set a fixed read date, and size each cell for the stated lift.

output_examples.input: Interpret two variants with supplied delivered and conversion counts.
output: Effect: reports the observed conversion-rate difference and uncertainty.
Decision status: applies the named precommitted rule only when an owner and rule are supplied.
Guardrails: identifies whether unsubscribe, complaint, or bounce thresholds were breached.

best_practices: Define one primary metric, a practical-effect threshold, and guardrails before sending.
Keep one variable isolated per cell and preserve a randomized control group.
Set the sample size and read date before the test, then avoid unplanned early decisions.
anti_patterns: Changing subject, creative, and send time in one test cell.
Calling a winner from an underpowered test or an early unplanned look.
Treating statistical significance as an automatic business decision without an approved rule.

faq.question: What test types can this skill plan?
faq.answer: It supports A/B, multivariate, send-time, and hold-out email experiments.

faq.question: What data do I need for a new test?
faq.answer: Provide a baseline rate, list size or daily volume, and the minimum lift worth detecting.

faq.question: What data do I need for a read-out?
faq.answer: Provide per-variant delivered counts and outcome counts, plus any relevant guardrail metrics.

faq.question: Can it choose a winning campaign automatically?
faq.answer: No. It applies an action only when you provide an owner and a precommitted decision rule.

faq.question: Does it create email copy?
faq.answer: No. It designs and evaluates experiments, but does not write the subject line, message body, or CTA.

faq.question: Does it require an email platform connection?
faq.answer: No. It can work from manually exported data. Platform connections are optional conveniences.
